e-7077.knowledge_point: Expanding a Statement by Distributing a Conjunction
e-7077.problem: Expand the statement $P \land (Q \lor R)$ by distributing the conjunction.
e-7077.worked_solution:
We distribute the conjunction over the disjunction, as follows:

$$
P \land (Q \lor R) \equiv (P \land Q) \lor (P \land R)
$$

e-7124.knowledge_point: Expanding a Statement by Distributing a Disjunction
e-7124.problem: Expand the statement $(C \land B) \lor A$ by distributing the disjunction.
e-7124.worked_solution:
We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

$$
(C \land B) \lor A  \equiv (C \lor A) \land (B \lor A)
$$

e-7078.knowledge_point: Simplifying a Statement Using the Distributive Property for Conjunctions
e-7078.problem: Simplify the statement $(A \land C) \lor (A \land B)$ using the distributive property for conjunctions.
e-7078.worked_solution:
We can factor out the conjunction with $A,$ as follows:

$$
(A \land C) \lor (A \land B) \equiv A \land (C \lor B)
$$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:

$$
P∧(Q∨R)≡(P∧Q)∨(P∧R)
$$

$$
(P∧Q)∨(P∧R)≡(Q∧P)∨(R∧P).
$$

after.worked_solution:

$$

(¬P∨¬Q)∧(¬P∨R)≡(¬P∨¬Q)∧(R∨¬P).
$$

Which statement is equivalent to (R∧P)∨Q?

a
(Q∧R)∧(P∨Q)
b
R∧(P∨Q)
c
(Q∨R)∨(P∧Q)
d
(Q∨R)∧(P∨Q)

(Q∨R)∧P
Submit

decision.explanation: Distributing disjunction gives (R∧P)∨Q ≡ (R∨Q)∧(P∨Q). Since R∨Q ≡ Q∨R, this matches option d.

after.name: Question 8
after.worked_solution:
We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

$$
(R∧P)∨Q≡(R∨Q)∧(P∨Q)
$$

Now, since $R∨Q≡Q∨R,$ we can write

$$
(R∨Q)∧(P∨Q)≡(Q∨R)∧(P∨Q).
$$

Question 10

Which statement is equivalent to (¬P∧Q)∨R?

a
(R∨P)∧(¬Q∨R)
b
(R∨¬P)∧(R∨Q)
c
¬P∧(R∨Q)
d
(R∨¬P)∨(R∨P)
e
(R∨¬P)∧Q
Submit

decision.explanation: Distributing disjunction over conjunction gives (¬P∧Q)∨R ≡ (¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R). Commuting both disjunctions yields option b.

after.name: Question 10
after.worked_solution:
We distribute the disjunction over the conjunction, as follows:

$$
(¬P∧Q)∨R≡(¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)
$$

Now, since $¬P∨R≡R∨¬P$ and $Q∨R≡R∨Q$ we can write

$$
(¬P∨R)∧(Q∨R)≡(R∨¬P)∧(R∨Q).
$$
